name: Pennsylvania Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Cheesesteaks to Pierogies
description:
Pennsylvania's restaurants, from a South Philly cheesesteak to a Lancaster smorgasbord.

Pennsylvania Eats is a free guide to eating in Pennsylvania: 56 cheesesteak, roast pork and hoagie counters, 36 tomato pie and Old Forge pizzerias and 6 Pennsylvania Dutch dining rooms we checked by hand, plus 23,362 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in nine regions, from Philadelphia and Pittsburgh to Lancaster, Scranton and Erie. No account, no ads.

PENNSYLVANIA GUIDES
• Cheesesteaks, Roast Pork & Hoagies: Philadelphia's steak shops, roast pork and hoagie counters.
• Tomato Pie & Old Forge Pizza: square tomato pie and Old Forge-style trays.
• Pennsylvania Dutch: family-style dining rooms and smorgasbords.
• Pennsylvania Icons: 18 places with a MICHELIN distinction or a James Beard honor.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by list.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "roast pork", "old forge", "smorgasbord lancaster".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every place on the Pennsylvania lists was checked in business in October 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source: a newspaper, a tourism guide or its own site. The rest come from Overture Maps open data and the City of Philadelphia's food licenses. Pennsylvania has no statewide restaurant grade, so each place links the inspecting agency's own search. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Pennsylvania Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture or the City of Philadelphia), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Pennsylvania Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Pennsylvania (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: 56 cheesesteak, roast pork and hoagie counters, 36 tomato pie and Old Forge pizzerias and Pennsylvania Dutch dining rooms, each checked in business in October 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus 18 MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 23,362 restaurants, cafés and bars statewide from open map data and the City of Philadelphia's food licenses. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Cheesesteaks, Roast Pork & Hoagies (or Tomato Pie & Old Forge Pizza, Pennsylvania Dutch, Pennsylvania Icons, Oldest Taverns & Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the inspecting agency's own search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("roast pork", "old forge", "smorgasbord lancaster").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Pennsylvania (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Pennsylvania, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "PA Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Pennsylvania Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Pennsylvania Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the City of Philadelphia's food licenses (a public record); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news. Inspection reports are not copied: each place links the agency's own public search.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/pennsylvania-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Pennsylvania; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection grades and computes none. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
